newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks snap losing streak.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks snap losing streak.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks snapped a four-session losing streak to climb back above 6,000 Friday, bond prices rose and the dollar hit a 33-month high against the Japanese yen.
Crude oil rose and gold edged lower.
Stocks got a boost from an unexpectedly strong earnings report from Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co., one of the 30 issues in the Dow Jones industrial average.
The Dow index rose 14.54 to 6,007.02 after falling 44 points on Thursday and ending below 6,000 for the first time in two weeks. For the week, the index lost 87.21 points.

"Investors are taking a stand at the 6,000 mark and there's a normal adjustment to the sell-off of recent sessions," said Jim Solloway, director of research at Argus Research. He noted the market got a lift from 3M, whose gains accounted for about nine points of the Dow's rise.
In the broader market, losers led gainers, 1,247 to 1,076, on moderate volume of about 365 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index fell 4.40 points to close at 1,222.60.

Stocks were pressured from the start after bond prices fell on news that orders for expensive manufactured goods rose a surprisingly strong 4.6 percent last month, the biggest jump since December 1992.
But bonds later rebounded after investors saw that most of the jump came from a big rise in aircraft orders, which fluctuate widely from month to month.
The rally in the bond market lent support to stocks as long-term interest rates fell.
The 30-year Treasury bond added 14/32, or $4.375 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, to 6.82 percent from 6.85 percent on Thursday.

3M surged $3.125 to $74.375, and touched a 52-week high of $74.50, after the company said earnings rose 16 percent in the third quarter, its first since spinning off the data storage and imaging businesses that had restrained 3M's results.

Trading slowed in the afternoon as Wall Street braced for next week's reports on third-quarter labour costs and October consumer confidence, both due on Tuesday, the first look at the economy in the third quarter, due on Wednesday, and Friday's key October jobs report.
Analysts said the market was likely to remain under pressure unless there is surprisingly good news.
In currency market, the dollar ended mixed against European currencies but rallied against the yen after a roller-coaster session.
The dollar closed at 1.5200 German marks, up from 1.5177 late on Thursday. Against the yen, the dollar finished at 113.42, its highest close since January 1994, up from 112.81 yen late on Thursday.
Crude oil for December delivery rose 35 cents to $24.86 a barrel at the New York Mercantile Exchange.
December gold fell 30 cents to $384.60 an ounce on New York's Commodity Exchange.
Overseas, London's FTSE index rose 23.0 to 4,022.4, but lost 30.7 points for the week. Tokyo's Nikkei average fell 263.52 points to end at 20,739.97 and was off 872.33 from last week.
